4 out of 5 stars — Quick and careful screen repair
Last week I dropped my phone on the sidewalk, and the front glass cracked
badly
across one corner. I stopped by Peak Mobile Repair on a Saturday morning without booking anything first, hoping someone could look at it right away. The shop was busier than I expected, and as a walk-in I waited close to an hour before anyone was free.
Once my turn came, the technician got straight to work. He replaced the shattered glass with a genuine manufacturer part, then fitted a fresh protector over the new screen. Before returning the phone, he cleared the dust out of my charging port, which had stopped holding a cable, and ran a quick check that included a battery test. The battery still held a full charge, so no replacement was needed. He handled the whole job with genuine care and finished in about two hours. The bill came to $80, and the new screen carries a 90-day guarantee, which put my mind at ease.
Although the repair itself could not have gone better, anyone who values their time would do well to secure an appointment rather than turn up unannounced as I did. The waiting area was cramped, and standing around for an hour was the only real drawback of an otherwise smooth visit.
— Gavin Holt

A Shoemaker Steps Into Recycled Materials
By Harriet Voss, March 12
Underhill Footwear has spent decades building a name for sturdy, handmade shoes. --[1]--.
The business began in 1994 in the coastal town of Kestrel Bay, where its founders opened a modest workshop above a hardware store. Within a decade the workshop had moved into a larger factory, and a small design team was added. --[2]--.
This spring the company introduced its first line made entirely from recycled materials. --[3]--. The shoes use uppers woven from reclaimed ocean plastic and soles pressed from ground rubber; even the laces are made without any new fibers.
Underhill plans to convert its entire range to recycled inputs by 2028. "We want every shoe we make to have a second life built into it," said design director Vincent Ordway. --[4]--. The recycled collection can be viewed and purchased at the company's new retail counter on Marlow Street.
This feature appears in the spring issue of Ledger & Loom.

Meadowgate Board Game Café — Member Bulletin
Spring Edition | February 20
Dear Meadowgate members,
We are pleased to introduce our new Game Lending Library, a free service that lets you borrow board games from our shelves and enjoy them at home for a full week. Library membership is included at no extra cost with your café membership, our way of thanking you for being part of the community.
To celebrate, we are holding a launch session on Saturday, March 8. Drop by for a short demonstration of how borrowing works, sample three featured titles at the tables, and sign up to take your very first game home that afternoon.
No reservation is needed. Simply show your membership card at the front counter when you arrive, and a staff member will help you get started.
Warm regards,
Trevor Blanchard, Café Manager
Open daily, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. | www.meadowgatecafe.example
----------------------
Reviewer: tabletop_gwen
Member since: 2021
Date of visit: March 8
Rating: 4 out of 5 stars
Would recommend: Yes
Comment: The launch was well organized, and the staff were patient about explaining everything. I borrowed a strategy game to take home, and checking it out at the counter was quick and simple. Two things would make the service even better: first, please give members a way to set aside popular titles before coming in, since the most-wanted games are snapped up quickly; and second, consider letting us keep a game for two weeks rather than a single week. My one complaint is that the display shelves were crowded and hard to browse.
----------------------
To: Meadowgate members
From: Trevor Blanchard
Date: March 12
Subject: Library news
Dear members,
Thank you to everyone who came to the Game Lending Library launch on March 8. The turnout was wonderful, and we are pleased to tell you about several changes to the library and the café.
Members can now reserve any available game through our website and collect it on their next visit. In addition, on Saturdays and Sundays the café will now stay open until 11 p.m., giving everyone more time to play. We have also added twenty new titles to the lending collection.
Looking ahead, we plan to open a second Meadowgate café in the Brookfield district this summer, where the lending library will be offered as well. We hope it will bring the service closer to many more of you.
Sincerely,
Trevor Blanchard
Questions? Write to us at
[email protected]

What We Do
We supply, install, and maintain exercise equipment for workplaces of every size. Whether you need a single stretching corner or a fully equipped staff wellness room, our team delivers each machine, assembles it on site, and trains your employees to use it safely before we leave.
Care Plans
Every order includes a choice of three care plans: Core, Active, and Total Care. All three cover parts and labor for a full year after installation. Only Total Care adds two complimentary maintenance visits each year. On the Core and Active plans, any maintenance visit is arranged and billed separately. You may upgrade your plan at any time, and to discuss which plan suits your workplace, contact our care team; a specialist will respond within two business days.
Specialist Spotlight
Our resistance equipment is designed in house by Naomi Beckett, who has shaped every strength-training station in our current range. Each unit she develops is engineered to withstand heavy daily use in busy shared spaces.
